steps.description: Re-derived all three measurements. (a) PRELOAD, guidance_report --check: constitution 4,112/4,200; project-guidance 3,928/3,930; lessons-learned 2,493/2,504; AGENTS.md 2,208/2,031 (OVER 177); TOTAL 12,741/12,600 (OVER 141). The spec's 2026-08-11 table (11,856/12,000, +144 headroom) is STALE -- a finding about the SPEC, and one it predicted: ceilings were raised under the standing operator authorization and the corpus grew, so headroom is now NEGATIVE (-141), not +144. (b) ACTIVE LESSONS: still five, but not the spec's five. Actual: L-064-8, L-064-9, L-079-1, L-112-1, L-125-1. L-075-1 was archived by Set 125 Step 9 (unused since Set 084); L-125-1 was admitted in its place. L-069-1 did NOT return to the active tier. A finding about the SPEC, which warned 'do not take the number five from this spec'. (c) PATH CITATION, classified by the shipped is_doc_only_issue/is_documentation_path over all 60 sets' sN-issues*.json: keyed on SET NUMBER the spec's '057-117 = 0 citing' is wrong (sets 115 and 118 cite paths); keyed on EXECUTION TIME it is exactly right -- before Set 119 S1 landed (2026-08-10T19:39) 0 of 572 findings cite paths, on/after 85 of 85 do (100%). Sets 115 and 118 were EXECUTED after 119; set numbers are allocation order, not execution order. So this discrepancy is about the QUERY, not the spec's claim, and the claim is now 6.5x better evidenced. Doc-only findings: still 0 of 85 -- the cap has never fired. Mixed doc+code: 38 of 85 (45%), up from the spec's 5 of 13 (38%), which strengthens the spec's named failure mode for Session 4.

Applied the operator rule (impact x likelihood vs work) to the RE-DERIVED five and journaled six decisions to decisions.jsonl. L-064-9 = CODE, already encoded (verify_session EvidenceBundle.git_status rendered before the diff; true falsifier confirmed). L-125-1 = CODE, already encoded (cli_transport READ_ONLY_TOOLS/_tool_grant_argv; true falsifier plus an 'assert granted' tripwire). L-112-1 = SPLIT: CODE for its empty-corpus bullet (proposal 5.2's full meta-gate is unbuildable -- pattern gates have no registry to enumerate -- but corpus scans ARE recognisable by shape, and ~6 offenders exist today so the gate fires on day one and self-applies), ONE LINE for the falsifier-per-rule remainder. L-079-1 = ONE LINE, a journaled DEVIATION from 5.2's 'code': the data-loss half is already encoded so a lint there scans a clean corpus, and the subprocess-pipe half is 29 sites whose correct fix is not uniform (git/podman emit UTF-8; the 7 powershell/tasklist children emit the console codepage, so a blanket encoding='utf-8' would newly break them) -- residual named. L-064-8 = ONE LINE, agreeing with 5.2; no mechanical corpus exists for semantic doc-claim checking.

Encoded L-112-1's empty-corpus bullet as ai_router/corpus_scan_guard.py -- an AST analyzer that refuses any test_* function walking the checked-out repo without asserting the walk matched anything. It is structural, not textual: it follows assignment through helpers, path-provider functions and intermediate variables, and it distinguishes the repo (module-level constants minted from __file__) from fixture trees, so the legitimate 'assert this wrote nothing' class stays legal. Building it surfaced two of its own false readings, both fixed and both now falsified: ast.walk was matching as a filesystem walk, and a fixture-rooted scan was being flagged. It found 5 real vacuous-pass tests on the day it shipped (test_no_legacy_field_reads, test_packaging_hygiene, test_production_imports x2, test_step_status_vocabulary); all 5 fixed by asserting the corpus, one via a small refactor so the assertion uses the gate's OWN corpus definition. Falsifiers: ai_router/tests/test_corpus_scan_guard.py, 13 tests -- 5 planted violations that must fire (including the two vacuous shapes 'assert all(...)' and 'assert offenders == []'), 5 planted look-alikes that must not, self-application (the gate asserts its own corpus is non-empty and names required members), and an entry-point agreement test. 83 tests green across the new module and the 4 edited ones. Guidance: L-064-9 and L-125-1 archived with encoded-in pointers; L-112-1, L-079-1 and L-064-8 condensed to one instruction line each with full text preserved trailerless in lessons-archive.md. TOKENS FREED: lessons-learned.md 2,493 -> 2,229 (264 freed, 89% of its 2,504 ceiling); preload TOTAL 12,741 -> 12,477, which clears the 12,600 total ceiling that was breached by 141 at session start. Residual: AGENTS.md remains 177 over its 2,031 ceiling -- pre-existing, outside this session's Touches, and covered by the standing operator authorization that Session 4 Step 3 retires.

Four rounds, VERIFIED at round 4 with 5 fix verdicts accepted and 0 findings. Verifier gpt-5.5 (anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's effective provider). Round 1 discovery (2-lens fan-out): 4 Majors, all accepted -- non-transitive helper detection (x2), lazy-iterator truthiness accepted as non-empty proof, and local Path(__file__) roots undetected. Round 2 supplementary: 1 Major, accepted -- pytest fixture-injected corpora bypass the guard entirely, including the conftest.py case where the parameter list is the only evidence. Round 3 remediation-review: 3 accepted / 1 rejected plus 1 new Major, accepted -- laziness was not propagated across the call boundary, so a helper returning a bare rglob still earned a vacuous 'assert files'. Round 4: VERIFIED. Every finding was a real false negative in the guard, and the root cause was the same each time: the guard had been calibrated against the corpus that exists today, which is the exact failure L-112-1 describes -- committed while encoding L-112-1. NOTE: the generated acceptance-criterion commands are unrunnable (a shell-escaping defect in the verifier's python -c "exec('...')" one-liners makes them raise SyntaxError before testing anything), so the harness reported still-failing on substance it never evaluated. The artifacts were NOT edited; each criterion's intent was reproduced as a runnable equivalent and run against both trees -- pre-fix trees taken from the git index and from the harness's own recorded round-2 tree. All 7 criteria fail pre-fix and pass post-fix, with every paired look-alike silent on both trees. Evidence tables are in s1-remediation-round-1.md and -round-3.md.

All three governed suites run in full after the last code change and recorded via run_of_record. run_of_record affected named all three: every suite declares ai_router/ in its covers, and this session changed ai_router/corpus_scan_guard.py plus six test modules. pytest: 4544 passed, 9 skipped, 594s. mocha (npm run test:unit): 1456 passing, 2 pending, 46s. playwright (npm run test:playwright): 32 passed, 332s. No failures anywhere; no baseline exclusions needed.

Close-out. The close backstop bought round 5 and found one Major -- a FALSE POSITIVE this time, the mirror of rounds 1-3: the round-3 laziness propagation did not stop at a materializing call, so files = list(_sources()) would have been reported as an offender though it is a real list. Fixed by _materializes(), stated once and applied at both decision points; three falsifiers added and the three round-3 violation falsifiers still pass, so propagation was corrected rather than switched off. The bounded 2 remediation-review cycles were then spent, leaving that shipped-code fix without settling evidence -- an operator stop, since manual-verify reduces verification and cannot be self-authorized. Operator authorized exactly one more round; round 6 returned VERIFIED with 6 fix verdicts accepted and 0 findings, and the authorization is recorded in s1-rounds.jsonl and decisions.jsonl. All three suites then re-run after the last code change: pytest 4547 passed / 9 skipped 547s, mocha 1456 passing / 2 pending 40s, playwright 32 passed 309s.

Moved usage accounting out of the preload corpus into ai_router/guidance_ledger.py -> docs/planning/guidance-usage.json: schemaVersion 1, keyed by id, {kind, cost, uses[]} with a bounded 10-entry ring of dash-separated zero-padded <set>-<session> STRINGS, one sanctioned writer, atomic replace, and the repo's single lock implementation via a new generic close_lock.file_mutex (the session-set lifecycle lock is directory-scoped and carries a Set-036 dual-hold, so exposing the proven stale-reclaim/TTL primitive beat growing a second copy of it). MEASUREMENT RE-DERIVED, and the spec's number is stale in the direction Session 1 left it: the spec says 'six trailers, 594 bytes, ~148 tokens', but after Session 1 archived two lessons and condensed three there are THREE trailers, 300 bytes, ~75 tokens (plus 5 lesson-pointer comments, 225 bytes, ~57 tokens). A finding about the SPEC. Every site redirected per L-069-1, not the first found: guidance_meta (last-used-set removed from LessonMeta/SINGLE_FIELDS/CANONICAL_ORDER; update_last_used is now a loud NotImplementedError stub rather than a silent no-op that would drop a pinned consumer's usage signal; normalize_close_mandated_metadata DELETED); cite_lessons (records to the ledger, resolves against the docs read-only, CLOSE_MANDATED_WRITES repointed to the ledger as whole-file); guidance_triage (the routed classifier now sees the real recency ring instead of the scalar); lessons-learned.md, lessons-archive.md, both consumer-bootstrap templates, the cold-start fixture and the extension dist bundle (npm run compile). status="active" is now omitted too, since the active tier is what active means. BACKFILLED from history rather than started empty: close_session has recorded disposition.lessons_cited into session-events.jsonl since Set 064, so 167 per-SESSION citation events across 65 sets seeded 25 ids with true recency rings -- strictly more than the scalar could hold. STRICTLY SAFER CLOSE EXEMPTION: the two preload documents lost their surgical exemption entirely and now bind byte for byte; only the bookkeeping JSON is exempt. Tokens: lessons-learned.md 2,229 -> 2,202.

Instruction-line retention in ACTIVE SESSIONS, never elapsed time. guidance_ledger.active_session_timeline() builds the denominator from closeout_succeeded events across every set, ordered by TIMESTAMP rather than by set number -- Session 1 measured sets 115 and 118 executing after 119, so a set-number sort would put a session in the window that had not run yet. 345 active sessions on record. A session that closed more than once (a repaired close) counts once, at its first success. retention_report() classifies retain / prune-candidate / never-used and there is deliberately NO evict path in the module: pruning is a batched pass the operator initiates, never automatic and never mid-session (standing decision 3), so the tool cannot perform the eviction that broke the old scheme. Scoping fix caught while wiring it: governed_ids scopes the INSTRUCTION rule to the live corpus only -- encoding a lesson is precisely what archives its prose, so scoping a check by corpus membership would exempt every check the moment it did its job.

Check retention split by cost, recording FIRES and not runs. Cheap (<1s, deterministic, no routed call) -> permanent, no usage record required, free insurance that never expires. Expensive (a routed call, or >10s) -> must have fired within the last N sets; never firing is reported as never-used rather than silently passing, because a gate that never fires is indistinguishable from a useless one, which IS L-112-1. 'Record fires, not runs' is ENCODED as a type error, not a convention: record_citation() refuses an executable and record_fire() refuses an instruction, so a CI run cannot be filed as a fire and a check cannot earn credit for being mentioned. Session 1's three encoded checks registered cheap: L-064-9, L-125-1, and K-121-1 (corpus_scan_guard -- a new check-namespace id, since L-112-1 survives as an instruction line and the check is a separate artifact).

N and the cap DERIVED from 345 sessions of citation history, not inherited from 5.3. (a) instruction_window_sessions = 30: measured over 694 intra-lesson gaps -- median 1, p90 5, p95 10, p99 30.2, max 51 -- so 30 retains 99% of genuinely recurring guidance through its quiet stretches. At this repo's measured 2.88 sessions/set that is ~10.4 sets, so 5.3's proposed 'N = 10 sets' SURVIVES measurement once the unit is corrected to the one the operator mandated. (b) check_window_sets = 20: the data supports NOTHING here -- there is no fire history at all, since the ledger records its first fire after this session -- so per the spec's instruction this is an honest default with a stated reason rather than a fabricated derivation: it reuses the operator-set disuse_window_sets of 20 that Set 064 already blessed, so the repo carries one disuse horizon rather than two that drift. (c) instruction_line_cap = 22: peak distinct ids cited in ANY trailing window across the whole history (20 at W=30, 21 at W=40-51, 22 at W=60-80), so 5.3's proposed 20 is close to the measured ceiling. KNOWN BLIND SPOT stated rather than smoothed over: project-guidance.md has no ids yet, so its ~24 entries contributed nothing to this measurement, which is exactly why Session 3 exists; Session 3 must RE-DERIVE the cap against the enlarged corpus rather than inherit 22 -- the same refusal this session made of 5.3.

Four rounds, VERIFIED at round 4 with 8 fix verdicts (7 accepted, 1 accepted-with-modification) and 0 findings. Verifier gpt-5.5; anthropic excluded as the orchestrator's registry-resolved effective provider on every round. Round 1 discovery (2-lens fan-out): 7 Majors. Round 2 supplementary: 1 Major. SEVEN ACCEPTED AND FIXED, ONE REJECTED AS A FALSE POSITIVE with evidence. Accepted: (1+3, one root cause) retention_report and instruction_count iterated the LEDGER, so a live instruction line with no ledger entry -- a brand-new lesson, or Session 3's project-guidance ids -- was neither reported nor counted against the cap; the anti-rebloat gate could pass on a corpus it could not see, and the case it missed is the case it exists to govern. (2) docs/ai-led-session-workflow.md Step 9 still taught the retired last-used-set/disuse_window_sets rule -- L-065-1, I fixed six echoes and missed the canonical procedure doc. (4) project-guidance readiness was only half real: corpus_ids used the HEADING-BOUND parser against a file whose entries are bullets under level-3 sections, so it would have returned zero ids SILENTLY, which is L-112-1's exact shape. (5) cite_lessons recorded unknown ids before reporting them, and since the module has no eviction path a typo became a permanent ghost. (6) --session defaulted to 1 silently -- a call I made deliberately and got wrong. (8, round 2, the sharpest) backfill+register let an executable INHERIT its prose-era citations, which retention_report reads as FIRES: an expensive check that had never caught anything would be retained for having once been prose somebody mentioned -- the exact failure the fire/run split exists to prevent, committed in the session that wrote the split. REJECTED (7): the claim that the shipped ledger's L-064-12 use '122-02' contradicts the close events. It does not -- set 122 session 2 cites L-064-12 and session 3 does not; the sessions are transposed. The ring's ordering was independently re-verified against close timestamps and is strictly descending by EXECUTION time (122-02 ahead of 127-02 and 123-03), which is the allocation-vs-execution property Session 1 measured. Evidence tables in s2-remediation-round-2.md. Round 3 rejected the project-guidance fix, CORRECTLY and for the same root cause one sibling site on: validate_documents still walked the heading-bound model and validate_guidance_meta still defaulted to the two lessons files, so the gate that must catch a malformed or duplicate project-guidance id would have reported success having inspected none of them -- L-069-1 twice in one session. Fixed with scan_entries() plus project-guidance in the default file set (the real corpus now validates 29 ids across 3 files, up from 26 across 2). Round 4: VERIFIED. HARNESS NOTE: round 1 finding #2 reported still-failing on a criterion whose expectedOutputContains carries stray literal double-quote characters, which no output can contain -- the Set 121 S1 defect class. The artifact was NOT edited; the criterion's intent was reproduced as a runnable equivalent and run against both trees (pre-fix produced '0 / cap', post-fix '1 / cap'), and running the verifier's own command exposed a real over-correction of mine: exiting non-zero on unregistered ids would have failed every fresh consumer repo, since a repo that has not cited anything has no ledger at all. Softened to surface-and-count, with a look-alike falsifier proving the cap still fires. Falsifiers proven non-vacuous by mutation: five rules mutated (string check, ring cap, kind guard, retention window, timestamp sort), all five fired.

All three governed suites run in full after the last code change and recorded via run_of_record. run_of_record affected named all three: every suite declares ai_router/ in its covers. pytest: 4631 passed, 9 skipped, 786s. mocha (npm run test:unit): 1456 passing, 2 pending, 33s. playwright (npm run test:playwright): 32 passed, 294s. TWO REAL FAILURES WERE FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE THESE RUNS, both from surfaces the targeted runs did not cover. (1) The extension's dist template bundle drifted once the consumer-bootstrap templates were edited; drift_guard named the remedy itself (npm run compile) and it was applied. (2) The mocha cold-start snapshot compares the RENDERED consumer-bootstrap template byte-for-byte against test-fixtures/cold-start/full/, and my hand-edit of the fixture wrapped two paragraphs differently from the template, so the golden was regenerated from the template with the fixed context substituted rather than hand-patched -- which is the deliberate, reviewed regeneration that test exists to force. HARNESS FINDING, not a product regression: the first playwright run was launched concurrently with the full pytest suite and reported 8 failures across unrelated tree-rendering specs (blocked-by-prereqs, cancellation, scaffold, icon-render, manifest-diagnostic, migration-drift, vsix-first-run). Re-run alone with no code change in between, the same suite returned 32 passed in 4.9m. Layer 3 drives a real VS Code UI on wall-clock timeouts, so it must not share a machine with a 4,600-test Layer 1 run; the recorded run is the uncontended one.
